questions.q: According to the Controlled Substances Act, which schedule is designated for drugs that have a high potential for abuse, no currently accepted medical use in the United States, and a lack of accepted safety for use under medical supervision?
questions.explain: Schedule I drugs (e.g., heroin, LSD, marijuana) are strictly regulated because they have no accepted medical use and a very high potential for abuse.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Toxicology & Pharmacology
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: What is the primary difference between a Schedule I drug and a Schedule II drug according to the federal Controlled Substances Act?
options: Schedule II drugs have a higher potential for abuse than Schedule I drugs.
Schedule II drugs have a currently accepted medical use with severe restrictions, whereas Schedule I drugs have no accepted medical use.
Schedule I drugs are available over the counter, while Schedule II drugs require a prescription.
There is no difference; they are classified together for law enforcement purposes.
questions.explain: Both Schedule I and II drugs have a high potential for abuse, but Schedule II drugs (like morphine, cocaine, and methamphetamine) have accepted medical uses under severe restrictions.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Toxicology & Pharmacology
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: Under the Controlled Substances Act, in which schedule are anabolic steroids classified?
questions.explain: Anabolic steroids are classified as Schedule III drugs. They have moderate to low potential for physical and psychological dependence compared to Schedule I or II.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Toxicology & Pharmacology
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: Which class of drugs is primarily known to alter normal thoughts, perceptions, and moods?
questions.explain: Hallucinogens, such as LSD and PCP, profoundly alter sensory perceptions, mood, and cognitive processes.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Toxicology & Pharmacology
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: Cocaine is extracted from the leaves of the Erythroxylum coca plant. Based on its physiological effects on the central nervous system, how is cocaine classified?
questions.explain: Cocaine is a powerful central nervous system stimulant that increases alertness, energy, and blood pressure.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Toxicology & Pharmacology
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: In forensic pharmacology, a 'narcotic' is strictly defined as a drug that:
options: Stimulates the central nervous system to prevent fatigue.
Enhances physical performance and muscle growth.
questions.explain: Medically and pharmacologically, a narcotic (opiate/opioid) is an analgesic that suppresses the central nervous system to relieve pain and induce sleep.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Toxicology & Pharmacology
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: Heroin is a highly addictive Schedule I narcotic. It is a semi-synthetic derivative created by reacting which naturally occurring opiate with acetic anhydride?
questions.explain: Heroin (diacetylmorphine) is synthesized by the acetylation of morphine, which is extracted from the opium poppy.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Toxicology & Pharmacology
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: Which of the following pairings represents drugs that both belong to the stimulant classification?
questions.explain: Both methamphetamine and cocaine increase central nervous system activity, making them stimulants.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Toxicology & Pharmacology
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: Depressants like barbiturates and benzodiazepines largely exert their calming and sleep-inducing effects by enhancing the activity of which neurotransmitter?
questions.explain: Depressants typically work by acting as agonists on GABA receptors, the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain, thus depressing the CNS.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Toxicology & Pharmacology
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: Fentanyl is a synthetic opioid responsible for many overdose deaths. Approximately how much more potent is fentanyl compared to morphine?
options: It is exactly equal in potency to morphine
questions.explain: Fentanyl is a synthetic narcotic analgesic estimated to be 50 to 100 times more potent than morphine.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Toxicology & Pharmacology
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: Which schedule of drugs includes preparations containing limited quantities of certain narcotics, such as cough syrups with a low dosage of codeine, and has the lowest potential for abuse?
questions.explain: Schedule V drugs have the lowest potential for abuse among the scheduled substances and generally consist of preparations containing limited quantities of certain narcotics.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Toxicology & Pharmacology
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: 'Bath salts' are a class of designer drugs often found in forensic casework. They are pharmacologically classified primarily as:
questions.explain: Bath salts contain synthetic cathinones, which are amphetamine-like stimulants that often also induce hallucinogenic effects.
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Toxicology & Pharmacology
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: MDMA (Ecstasy) is uniquely classified because it shares pharmacological properties of both:
questions.explain: MDMA increases alertness and energy (stimulant) while also altering sensory perception and time (hallucinogen).
questions.exam: HOSA Forensic Science: Forensic Toxicology & Pharmacology
questions.subject: Forensic Science

questions.q: Club drugs such as GHB and Rohypnol are often implicated in drug-facilitated sexual assaults. To which drug class do these substances belong?
questions.explain: GHB and Rohypnol are central nervous system depressants that can cause drowsiness, muscle relaxation, and amnesia.
